title: Genesis Primitives are single-Invocation by construction, permanently closing their Invocation directory after use
content:
Every Genesis Primitive in Obex's Artifact replaces the standard In Progress Invocations text with a closure statement. The Agent Creation Primitive "is deployed solely for the one-time creation of the Agent, [so] no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.1.4); the same wording appears for Prime Transformation (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.2.1.4), Executor Transformation (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.3.1.4) and, in token form, the Agent Token Primitive (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.4.1.4).

Contrast the Executor Accord Primitive at A.6.1.1.5.2.2.1.1.4, which keeps the generic lifecycle language: successful Invocations move to Active Instances, failed ones are archived in the Hub Data Repository. Operational Primitives remain re-Invocable; Genesis Primitives do not.

This is a one-way door encoded in the document structure itself. An Agent cannot be created twice, cannot re-run its transformation into a Prime, and cannot re-deploy its token. The Genesis Primitives collectively define identity, and identity is treated as non-repeatable.

The consequence is that Genesis Primitives carry a **Single Instance Configuration Document** rather than a directory of many, and their Operational Process Definition states that "no further operational process is needed post-deployment" (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.3.1.2). The document keeps the historical record but has no ongoing process attached — a genuinely different lifecycle shape from Primitives that describe continuing activity.
description: Agent Creation, Prime Transformation, Executor Transformation and Agent Token each declare that no further Instances can ever be Invoked
